# Summary

This shows some concepts related to Bayesian variable selection based off of the handbook by Tadesse and Vannucci (2021)[@tadesse2021handbook].

# Overview of Variable Selection in Bayesian Framework

```{r}
#| echo: false

library(DiagrammeR)

DiagrammeR(
 "graph TD
    A[Variable selection methods] --> B[Hypothesis Testing]
    A[Variable selection methods] --> C[Penalized Parameter Estimation]
    B[Hypothesis Testing] --> D[Bayes factor]
    B[Hypothesis Testing] --> E[Posterior Model Probabilities]
    C[Penalized Parameter Estimation] --> F[Shinkage priors that induce sparsity]
    F[Shinkage priors that induce sparsity] --> G[Spike-and-slab priors]
    F[Shinkage priors that induce sparsity] --> H[Continuous shrinkage priors]
    H[Continuous shrinkage priors] --> I[Horseshoe prior]
  "  )
    
```



Benefit:

- allow rich modeling via MCMC stochastic search strategies and incorporate optimal model averaging prediction
- extend naturally to multivariate responses and many linear and non-linear settings
- can handle the "small $n$-large $p$" setting, i.e., situations where the number of covariates is larger than the sample size;
- they allow the use of priors that incorporate past and collateral information into the model


# Discrete Spike-and-slab

A latent binary vector is introduced to index the possible subsets of predictors and
used to induce mixture priors of two components on the regression coefficients,
one peaked at zero (spike) and the other one a diffuse distribution (slab).
Posterior inference is carried out via stochastic search MCMC techniques to identify 
the high-probability models, and variable selection is performed based on the 
posterior model probabilities.

- discrete spike-and-slab constructions: employ a point mass distribution at zero as the spike component
